title: TUI Ink renderer and conversation surface iteration
objective: Adopt the high-upside Ink renderer / DOM-level TUI architecture from cc where it materially improves long-session performance, scroll fidelity, overlay layering, and operator ergonomics.
summary: Eight pending tasks: renderer substrate, virtual transcript, unseen divider, input overlays, transcript search, foldable message rendering, status/noise reduction, and cross-viewport performance gates.

waves.name: Renderer substrate
waves.description: Introduce the DOM-level scroll/render foundation before changing conversation behavior.

waves.name: Conversation virtualization
waves.description: Move transcript rendering onto virtualized scroll primitives and restore user-facing unseen-message behavior.

waves.name: Operator interaction surfaces
waves.description: Layer input overlays, search, foldable message rows, and service/status surfaces on top of the new substrate.

waves.name: Regression and performance gates
waves.description: Lock the new TUI behavior with viewport, scroll, search, and performance checks.

in: Ink renderer / DOM-level ScrollBox equivalent for Swarm TUI
Virtual transcript and render cache for long sessions
Unseen divider, sticky prompt, and jump-to-bottom semantics
Input overlay, modal gating, and footer pill navigation
Transcript search and message cursor actions
Foldable thinking/tool/result rows with inspector handoff
Default status noise reduction for cache, Gateway, Symphony, Swarm, and LSP
TUI viewport and performance regression gates
out: Gateway API redesign unrelated to TUI presentation

confidence.reason: The renderer substrate has high upside but also touches low-level TUI assumptions, so implementation cost and integration risk are higher than a pure line-windowing pass.
